Heard learned counsel for the appellant and Mr. Pradhan, learned ASC for the State.
2. No one appears for the informant, namely, opposite party No.2.It is submitted to the Court by Mr.
Pradhan, learned ASC that the notice stands served on opposite party No.2 in the meantime.
In view of the above, the Court is inclined to dispose of the petition by the following order.
3. Recording the submissions of the learned counsel for the respective parties.

4. Instant appeal is filed by the appellant seeking release on bail in connection with T.R. Case No.408 of 2023 corresponding to Air field P.S. Case No.192 dated 5th August, 2023 pending in the file of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Bhubaneswar on the grounds stated.

5. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant and the informant/victim, namely,
opposite party No.2, have had relationship for quite some time and when their marriage did not materialize, the report was lodged at last and considering the fact that there is closure of investigation, the accused should be allowed to go on bail subject to any terms and conditions as would be fixed by the Court.
6.

Mr. Pradhan, learned ASC for the State objects to the release of the appellant on bail for the fact that he declined to marry the victim, namely, opposite party No.2 after having kept relationship with her with a promise of marriage in future.

7. A copy of the statement of opposite party No.2 under Section 164 Cr.P.C. is produced before the Court along with the case diary and other police papers and the same are perused.
A copy of the chargesheet is also made available by learned counsel for the appellant and the same is perused.
8. From the materials on record, it is suggested that the parties had been in a relationship which is admitted by the informant/victim, namely, opposite party No.2.
It is made to appear that after having a relationship for some time, the appellant expressed his inability to marry the victim.
The matter was sought to be settled at the Panchayat level as revealed from the statement of opposite party No.2 under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
It is informed to the Court that in the meantime, opposite party No.2 has given birth to a child begotten from such relationship with the appellant.

Having regard to the above facts and the relationship in existence between the parties and that the investigation is concluded with the chargesheet being filed though under Section 376(2)(n) IPC and other allied offences, the Court is of the view that the appellant, who is in custody since the date of arrest, should be allowed to go on bail subject to following conditions.
9. Accordingly, it is ordered.
10. In the result, the petition stands allowed.

Consequently, the appellant is directed to be released on bail in connection with T.R Case No.408 of 2023 arising out of Air field P.S. Case No. 192 of 2023 subject to him furnishing a bail bond of Rs.50,000/-(rupees fifty thousand) with one solvent surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Bhubaneswar, who shall be at liberty to impose such other suitable conditions as deemed just and proper in the facts and circumstances of the case besides the following such as, he shall not cause any harm to opposite party No.2 in any manner, whatsoever, while on bail.
11. The BLAPL is disposed of.
12. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rules.

(R.K. Pattanaik) Judge kabita Tapu @ Biswa Prakash Jena vs State Of Odisha & Others on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/114963025/
